cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ResourceManager.as:41,186,200-214; verified by decrypting reference/extracted/android/115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin at key 104 -> valid CWS v17 SWF, 1,040,849 bytes inflated, 1,912 SymbolClass entries
lane_impact: Cross-lane extraction rule (art, audio, items): keys are 104/117/111/109/103 by resource, derived not guessed - anyone opening the remaining blobs can stop brute-forcing.
quote: ResourceManager.as:41 `internal static var resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"];` :186 `ba = decryptByteArray(ba,resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1));` :205 `for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++)` :207 `if(i % 11 == 0)` :213 `ba[i] ^= key;`
text: The XOR key for the five obfuscated Android resource blobs is NOT one constant - it is the SECOND CHARACTER of the resource's filename, so every blob has its own key. ResourceManager.as:186 passes 'resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1)' into decryptByteArray, and :41 lists the five filenames. That yields shs3resource.swf -> 'h' = 104, musicresource.swf -> 'u' = 117, soundresource.swf -> 'o' = 111, imageresource.swf -> 'm' = 109, bgresource.swf -> 'g' = 103. This reconciles the two keys the Stage-0 brief already carries (C1's 109 from Mobile.as:352 and C3's 111 for the sound blob) and predicts the other three. Also note decryptByteArray only touches bytes 3..255 (swapping every i%11==0 byte with i+256), which is why the files still begin with a readable 'CWS' magic.

lane_impact: Cross-lane, and it hardens ⚠ S0-3 from a hedge into a proven hazard: web and android combat/progression tuning demonstrably diverge on four of six stat caps.
text: A hard, measured counterexample to build parity, found while checking the 271-cap claim. The stat-panel add-button gates are the same function in both builds but carry DIFFERENT formulas. ATK/DEF/SPD: android InventoryUI.as:2410-2412 gate on 'charlevel + 10' (90 at level 80); web §1t5957s0§.as:3344-3346 gate on '1 + (level + 10) * 3' (271 at level 80) — a 3x lift. MAXHP: android :2407 '10 + (charlevel + 10) * 5' (460); web :3341 '10 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 10' (910) — doubled. MAXAP: android :2409 '20 + (charlevel + 10)' (110); web :3343 '30 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 5' (480) — more than 4x. MAXCHI is the only one identical: android :2408 and web :3342 are both '10 + (lvl + 10) * 5' = 460. This is exactly the shape of divergence the S0-3 caveat warns about, now with numbers: the data XMLs match row for row, but progression tuning does NOT. Any INFERRED progression number ported from an android artifact must be re-derived web-side before it is called CONTRACT.

lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: an argument-order bridge that names six web fields from android symbols without diffing a file against itself - reusable wherever a web/android pair shares a call signature.
text: C2 says the four data XMLs are android-side, so diffing them proves nothing, and that combat tuning parity is NOT established. Here is a bridge that is not circular. Android StatsManager.as:1834 calls `player.initPlayer(0, HP, MAXHP, CHI, MAXCHI, DEFENSE, getBaseReload(), getMinDamage(), getDamageRange(), getBaseSlashLength(), getSlashUsage(), getStat(1000), getStat(1001), getStat(1002), getLevel())` - fifteen named arguments. The web fighter's ctor §1t99s0§.as:188-201 takes exactly fifteen ints and assigns them in exactly that order, including `this.defense = param6` at the DEFENSE slot, which pins the alignment independently. That decodes six obfuscated web fields at once (§1t3257s0§=MAXHP, §1t4413s0§=MAXCHI, §1t4421s0§/§1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ = skills 1000/1001/1002, §1t4420s0§=baseSlashLength) and it is what actually rules out an off-by-one in the mastery term.

text: The packet notes that string 960 is unresolvable from the android table but not why, and the mechanism is a genuine, first-hand v0.717-vs-v0.682 divergence - one of the very few that discharges part of the C2 caveat instead of restating it. Android BattleUI.as:262 is the ENTIRE reload-bar text logic: `this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;` - the android build shows the crit text at full and nothing at all otherwise. It has no empty-state label on the bar. Instead its 'Change Stance' string lives on a mouse rollover over the portrait: :192-193 add MOUSE_OVER/MOUSE_OUT listeners on battlemodebust bound to showChangeStanceLabel/hideChangeStanceLabel (:430-440), which toggle changestancelabel and the bust highlight together. The web build replaced that hover affordance with a persistent on-bar notice, which is why getString(960) exists in v0.717 and is missing from the v0.682 table (strings.json["960"] returns None). Android also normalises the ratio itself before the call, while the web computes (reload-48)/(max-48) inside §1t5205s0§.

Android BattleUI.as:259-263 updateReload is two lines: 'this.reloadbar.bar.scaleX = percentage;' and 'this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;'. There is no ratio==0 branch and no second htmlText. The web v0.717 twin §1t113s0§.as:326-359 adds all three states (grey getString(960) at ratio 0, hidden at 0<r<1, black getString(175) + Snd_criticalDamage at r>=1) and rescales the input to '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' where android passes a pre-computed percentage.
